name: Lockheed P-38 Lightning
blurb: A twin-boom Army fighter, planned as a player-flown and friendly type.
history:
The Lockheed P-38 Lightning was a single-seat, twin-engined fighter built for the U.S. Army Air Corps, with a distinctive twin-boom layout and a central nacelle holding the cockpit and guns. Turbochargers on both engines made it one of the earliest Allied fighters to perform well at high altitude, and it also served as a fighter-bomber, night fighter, long-range escort and, with cameras in place of guns, a reconnaissance aircraft.

In the South West Pacific the P-38 was the Army Air Forces' main long-range fighter until large numbers of P-51D Mustangs arrived near the war's end. America's top aces, Richard Bong and Thomas McGuire among them, flew it.
